active_family: 652 candidate: shared-stochastic multi-head joint path model
current_bottleneck: The wide data framing is valid, but a homogeneous 38-channel decoder likely underfits heterogeneous observations, while source-affine variants break shared geometry. The next model should preserve one shared stochastic path/backbone and only specialize the observation readouts.
last_result_summary: 651a audited the unified IV+anchor factor data framing for 30/60/90/152-day horizons. Source panel is 5822x51; modeled state panel is 38 channels = 25 IV + 13 anchor state variables. Finite rates are 1.0, no test leakage is detected, and future state reconstruction from modeled one-day encoded increments has max error 0.0 for all audited horizons. Reference-return discrepancies up to 0.08 are diagnostics from source return/diff columns, not modeled-target reconstruction failures.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 652a as a shared-stochastic multi-head path flow: one history encoder, one stochastic source/path backbone, separate IV-surface and generic factor readout heads, and support both iv_only and joint38 scopes.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 612a is the highest IV-count native joint run at 6/11 but has a degenerate source-scale mechanism and poor anchor-factor joint audit. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 641a is the clean native joint baseline because it removes post-hoc gluing and recovers strong anchor-factor realism, but it is still only 4/11 on the IV suite.
oracle_feasibility_note: 435a reaches 11/11 only as a validation-future oracle upper bound; it is not a deployable or learned conditional scenario generator.
